questions.question: Which statement is a directly measurable criterion rather than a broad reasoning construct?
options: The system answers protected multi-step arithmetic items correctly under protocol version 3
questions.explanation: A criterion names observable tasks and conditions. Broad constructs such as mathematical reasoning need criteria and evidence before they can be measured.

questions.question: A model scores 90% on recall questions, but the product claim promises reliable troubleshooting. What evidence is still required?
options: Only more recall questions from the same source
Application items that represent new troubleshooting cases and critical failure slices
A larger font for the score
questions.explanation: Recall breadth does not establish transfer. The suite needs representative application tasks and enough evidence in decision-critical troubleshooting slices.

questions.question: What distinguishes a composite benchmark from an evaluation dashboard?
options: A composite benchmark applies an explicit rule that combines component evidence, while a dashboard may preserve dimensions without one universal score
A dashboard always contains fewer tasks
A composite benchmark never shows component results
questions.explanation: Aggregation is a policy choice. A dashboard can expose trade-offs without claiming that one scalar is sufficient.

questions.question: What is the core invariant of a valid A/B test?
options: The treatment receives more traffic than control
Groups are comparable before treatment and assignment remains stable
Every observed metric reaches statistical significance
The candidate has a higher offline model score
questions.explanation: Stable random assignment makes the groups comparable in expectation, so the planned treatment is the systematic difference the analysis can attribute outcomes to.
